**Zvec** is an open-source, in-process vector database — lightweight, lightning-fast, and designed to embed directly into applications. Battle-tested within Alibaba Group, it delivers production-grade, low-latency and scalable similarity search with minimal setup. > [!Important] > 🚀 **v0.8.0** > > - **Broader platform support**: Added **Intel Mac** and **Windows ARM64** builds, wheels, and SDKs; extended **DiskANN to Windows, Android, and iOS**, and **RaBitQ to Windows x86_64**. > - **Chinese FTS ready to use**: Embedded the default **Jieba dictionary and HMM model**, so Chinese tokenization needs no separate dictionary files or path configuration. > - **Lower index build costs**: Reduced peak memory during **IVF / DiskANN** builds and merges, and accelerated **HNSW RaBitQ** construction through vector reuse and batched lookups. Build and nested training tasks now enforce configured thread limits more strictly. > - **Faster distance computation**: Extensively refactored quantizers and distance calculations to benefit multiple quantization types and metrics, with major improvements to **INT4 kernels** and **Linux ARM64** performance. > - **Faster search**: Added faster **Uniform quantizers** and optimized **Vamana** graph layout and prefetching. Uniform quantization avoids per-point score reconstruction, though a shared min/max range can increase quantization error and reduce recall. > - **Bug fixes and improvements**: Added more flexible **UTF-8 document IDs** up to 1,024 bytes; fixed concurrent reads during segment switches, index rebuilding with deleted rows, and correctness issues in **LIKE** and floating-point range filters. > > 👉 [Read the Release Notes](https://github.com/alibaba/zvec/releases/tag/v0.8.0) [^query-performance]: Measured on GIST 1M with L2 distance, INT8 quantization, and HNSW on a 16-core Linux ARM64 system. ## 💫 Features - **Blazing Fast**: Searches billions of vectors in milliseconds. - **Simple, Just Works**: [Install](#-installation) and start searching in seconds. Pure local, no servers, no config, no fuss. - **Dense + Sparse Vectors**: Support dense and sparse embeddings, multi-vector queries, and a rich selection of [vector index types](https://zvec.org/en/docs/db/concepts/vector-index/#vector-index-types) that scale from memory to disk. - **Full-Text Search (FTS)**: Native keyword-based full-text search — query string fields with natural-language or structured expressions. - **Hybrid Search**: Fuse vector similarity, full-text search, and structured filters in a single query for precise results. - **Durable Storage**: Write-ahead logging (WAL) guarantees persistence — data is never lost, even on process crash or power failure. - **Concurrent Access**: Multiple processes can read the same collection simultaneously; writes are single-process exclusive. - **Runs Anywhere**: As an in-process library, Zvec runs wherever your code runs — notebooks, servers, CLI tools, or even edge devices. ## 📦 Installation Zvec offers official SDKs across multiple languages: | SDK | Install / Dependency | Source | | --- | --- | --- | | [Python](https://pypi.org/project/zvec/) | `pip install zvec` | [Source](https://github.com/alibaba/zvec/tree/main/python/zvec) | | [Node.js](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zvec/zvec) | `npm install @zvec/zvec` | [Source](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-node) | | [Go](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-go) | [Installation guide](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-go#installation) | [Source](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-go) | | [Rust](https://crates.io/crates/zvec-rust) | `cargo add zvec-rust` | [Source](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-rust) | | [Java](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/org.zvec/zvec-java) | `org.zvec:zvec-java` (Maven) | [Source](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-java) | | [Dart / Flutter](https://pub.dev/packages/zvec) | `flutter pub add zvec` | [Source](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-dart) | Python requires 64-bit Python 3.10–3.14; Java requires Java 8+. Searching code or documents? Try **[zvec-grep](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-grep)** (`zg`) — a local-first search CLI that unifies ripgrep, BM25, and vector search, built for humans and AI agents. Prefer a visual tool? Try **[Zvec Studio](https://github.com/zvec-ai/zvec-studio)** to browse data and debug queries — no code required. ### ✅ Cross-Platform Support **Linux · macOS · Windows · Android · iOS** Zvec supports all major platforms — from servers and desktops to mobile devices.
For more details, please see the [platform support documentation](https://zvec.org/en/docs/db/platforms/). ### 🛠️ Building from Source If you prefer to build Zvec from source, please check the [Building from Source](https://zvec.org/en/docs/db/build/) guide. ## ⚡ One-Minute Python Example ```python import zvec # Define collection schema schema = zvec.CollectionSchema( name="example", vectors=zvec.VectorSchema("embedding", zvec.DataType.VECTOR_FP32, 4), ) # Create collection collection = zvec.create_and_open(path="./zvec_example", schema=schema) # Insert documents collection.insert([ zvec.Doc(id="doc_1", vectors={"embedding": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]}), zvec.Doc(id="doc_2", vectors={"embedding": [0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.1]}), ]) # Search by vector similarity results = collection.query( zvec.Query(field_name="embedding", vector=[0.4, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1]), topk=10 ) # Results: list of {'id': str, 'score': float, ...}, sorted by relevance print(results) ``` ## 📈 Performance at Scale Zvec delivers exceptional speed and efficiency, making it ideal for demanding production workloads. English | 中文

🚀 Quickstart | 🏠 Home | 📚 Docs | 📊 Benchmarks | 🔎 DeepWiki | 🎮 Discord | 🐦 X (Twitter)

Zvec is an open-source, in-process vector database — lightweight, lightning-fast, and designed to embed directly into applications. Battle-tested within Alibaba Group, it delivers production-grade, low-latency and scalable similarity search with minimal setup.

Important

🚀 v0.8.0

  • Broader platform support: Added Intel Mac and Windows ARM64 builds, wheels, and SDKs; extended DiskANN to Windows, Android, and iOS, and RaBitQ to Windows x86_64.
  • Chinese FTS ready to use: Embedded the default Jieba dictionary and HMM model, so Chinese tokenization needs no separate dictionary files or path configuration.
  • Lower index build costs: Reduced peak memory during IVF / DiskANN builds and merges, and accelerated HNSW RaBitQ construction through vector reuse and batched lookups. Build and nested training tasks now enforce configured thread limits more strictly.
  • Faster distance computation: Extensively refactored quantizers and distance calculations to benefit multiple quantization types and metrics, with major improvements to INT4 kernels and Linux ARM64 performance.
  • Faster search: Added faster Uniform quantizers and optimized Vamana graph layout and prefetching. Uniform quantization avoids per-point score reconstruction, though a shared min/max range can increase quantization error and reduce recall.
  • Bug fixes and improvements: Added more flexible UTF-8 document IDs up to 1,024 bytes; fixed concurrent reads during segment switches, index rebuilding with deleted rows, and correctness issues in LIKE and floating-point range filters.

👉 Read the Release Notes

💫 Features

  • Blazing Fast: Searches billions of vectors in milliseconds.
  • Simple, Just Works: Install and start searching in seconds. Pure local, no servers, no config, no fuss.
  • Dense + Sparse Vectors: Support dense and sparse embeddings, multi-vector queries, and a rich selection of vector index types that scale from memory to disk.
  • Full-Text Search (FTS): Native keyword-based full-text search — query string fields with natural-language or structured expressions.
  • Hybrid Search: Fuse vector similarity, full-text search, and structured filters in a single query for precise results.
  • Durable Storage: Write-ahead logging (WAL) guarantees persistence — data is never lost, even on process crash or power failure.
  • Concurrent Access: Multiple processes can read the same collection simultaneously; writes are single-process exclusive.
  • Runs Anywhere: As an in-process library, Zvec runs wherever your code runs — notebooks, servers, CLI tools, or even edge devices.

📦 Installation

Zvec offers official SDKs across multiple languages:

SDK Install / Dependency Source
Python pip install zvec Source
Node.js npm install @zvec/zvec Source
Go Installation guide Source
Rust cargo add zvec-rust Source
Java org.zvec:zvec-java (Maven) Source
Dart / Flutter flutter pub add zvec Source

Python requires 64-bit Python 3.10–3.14; Java requires Java 8+.

Searching code or documents? Try zvec-grep (zg) — a local-first search CLI that unifies ripgrep, BM25, and vector search, built for humans and AI agents.

Prefer a visual tool? Try Zvec Studio to browse data and debug queries — no code required.

✅ Cross-Platform Support

Linux · macOS · Windows · Android · iOS

Zvec supports all major platforms — from servers and desktops to mobile devices.
For more details, please see the platform support documentation.

🛠️ Building from Source

If you prefer to build Zvec from source, please check the Building from Source guide.

⚡ One-Minute Python Example

import zvec

# Define collection schema
schema = zvec.CollectionSchema(
    name="example",
    vectors=zvec.VectorSchema("embedding", zvec.DataType.VECTOR_FP32, 4),
)

# Create collection
collection = zvec.create_and_open(path="./zvec_example", schema=schema)

# Insert documents
collection.insert([
    zvec.Doc(id="doc_1", vectors={"embedding": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]}),
    zvec.Doc(id="doc_2", vectors={"embedding": [0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.1]}),
])

# Search by vector similarity
results = collection.query(
    zvec.Query(field_name="embedding", vector=[0.4, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1]),
    topk=10
)

# Results: list of {'id': str, 'score': float, ...}, sorted by relevance
print(results)

📈 Performance at Scale

Zvec delivers exceptional speed and efficiency, making it ideal for demanding production workloads.

For detailed benchmark methodology, configurations, and complete results, please see our Benchmarks documentation.

releases.body:
# 🚀 Zvec v0.8.0 Release Notes
Zvec v0.8.0 brings **faster queries, lower index build costs, and broader platform support**. Quantizer and distance-kernel improvements benefit multiple formats and metrics, with major gains for INT4 and Linux ARM64. This release also reduces peak memory during IVF/DiskANN builds, accelerates HNSW RaBitQ construction, and makes Chinese FTS ready to use with embedded Jieba resources. Platform coverage expands across desktop and mobile, alongside fixes for concurrent reads, index rebuilding, and filtering correctness.

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes and Upgrade Notes
+ **Jieba global dictionary configuration removed:** Default dictionaries and the HMM model are now embedded in native libraries. Python users must remove `init(jieba_dict_dir=...)` and calls to `set_default_jieba_dict_dir()` / `get_default_jieba_dict_dir()`. The corresponding C configuration accessors, C default-directory APIs, and C++ global configuration field and registration APIs have also been removed. releases.name: v0.7.0
releases.body:
## 🚀 Zvec v0.7.0 Release Notes

### ⚠️ Breaking Changes
+ **C++ public API switched to snake_case:** All public C++ SDK interfaces (`Index`, `Collection`, etc.) have been moved from PascalCase to snake_case. For example, `Open()` → `open()`, `Search()` → `search()`, `Query()` → `query()`, and `Insert()` → `insert()`. C++ SDK users will need to update their call sites when upgrading. The C API and Python API names remain unchanged. ([#683](https://github.com/alibaba/zvec/pull/683))

### 📦 New Features
+ **IVF RaBitQ index:** Added RaBitQ quantization support for IVF indexes, extending RaBitQ to more dense-vector retrieval scenarios. C and Python bindings and test coverage are included. ([#540](https://github.com/alibaba/zvec/pull/540))
+ **Turbo preprocessor framework:** Introduced an optional preprocessor component in the Turbo quantizer module. Fast Hadamard Transform (FHT) rotation is implemented now, with OPQ rotation and dimensionality reduction planned for future releases. ([#548](https://github.com/alibaba/zvec/pull/548))

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, in-process vector database by Alibaba built for lightweight, low-latency similarity search.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Zvec is an embedded, purely local vector database designed to run entirely in-process alongside your application code, removing the need for a separate database server. Battle-tested internally at Alibaba, it seamlessly combines dense and sparse vector embeddings, native full-text search, and structured filters into unified hybrid queries. It leverages advanced indexing techniques like HNSW, DiskANN, and quantization (such as INT8/INT4 with random rotation) to achieve millisecond latency across billions of vectors. With write-ahead logging for durability and multi-process read concurrency, it scales efficiently from Jupyter notebooks to edge devices and production backends.
keyFeatures: In-Process Architecture: Embeds directly into applications without requiring external servers, complex configurations, or network overhead.
Hybrid Search Engine: Fuses dense vectors, sparse vectors, structured metadata filters, and native full-text search in a single query.
Advanced Quantization: Uses random rotation for INT8/INT4 quantization to distribute variance across dimensions, preserving high recall rates.
Group-By Retrieval: Enables retrieving top-K results per specific group (group-by deduplication) rather than just a global top-K list.
Durable Storage: Guarantees data persistence using Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), preventing data loss during process crashes or power failures.
Multi-Language Full-Text Search: Includes a Unicode UAX #29 tokenizer and Snowball-based stemming pipeline supporting over 34 languages.

useCases.title: Local RAG Applications
useCases.description: Building Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines inside desktop applications or edge devices without relying on external cloud vector databases.

useCases.title: Multi-Modal Search
useCases.description: Searching across text and image embeddings simultaneously using hybrid queries that blend vector similarity with exact keyword matches.

useCases.title: Fast Deduplication
useCases.description: Using group-by search capabilities to quickly filter and deduplicate vast datasets based on metadata categories.

useCases.title: Notebook Experimentation
useCases.description: Allowing data scientists to spin up and query billions of vectors directly from Jupyter notebooks with zero infrastructure setup.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Data scientists, AI engineers, and backend developers who need a blazing-fast, embedded vector search engine without the operational overhead of a standalone database cluster. It provides scalable vector database solutions.
